sections.h2: How can I sell my house in Lebanon, TN?
sections.html:
Owners in Lebanon have three realistic paths: hire an agent, find a buyer yourself, or let a cash buyer take the place in its current shape. Weigh the house's shape, your deadline and how much price you will trade for speed.

Lebanon has grown quickly. QuickFacts puts Lebanon at 53,412 people in mid-2025, a 38.8% jump over the April 2020 base of 38,495. Owners occupy 62.4% of housing units, their homes have a 2020-2024 median value of $378,400, and renters pay a median of $1,306.

  • A listing reaches the most buyers but runs on the buyer's inspection and loan schedule.
  • A private sale skips the agent fee and leaves the paperwork to you.
  • A cash purchase removes showings and repairs and lets you name the closing date.

sections.h2: Why is Lebanon, Tennessee attractive to buyers?
sections.html:
Lebanon serves as the Wilson County seat, about 25 miles east of downtown Nashville, and dates its incorporation to 1801, according to Wikipedia. Locals call it Cedar City after the red cedars that grow in the area. Cumberland University, founded in 1842, and the Nashville Superspeedway are two landmarks, and the Tennessee State Fair is held here with the Wilson County Fair.

Commuters shape demand. Interstate 40 runs south of the city with three Lebanon exits, U.S. 70 leads west to Nashville, and the WeGo Star commuter train ends in Lebanon with weekday service. Hartmann Drive and Maddox-Simpson Parkway form a partial beltway, and the typical Lebanon worker travels 27.0 minutes to work.

sections.h2: What drives the local economy in Lebanon?
sections.html:
Several large employers sit inside the city. Cracker Barrel was founded in Lebanon in 1969 and keeps its headquarters here, and Lochinvar, a water products maker, is also based in town. The Wonderful Group invested $150 million in a tile plant in 2015, its first manufacturing site in North America, and Tritium opened an electric vehicle fast-charger plant in 2022.

The historic Mitchell House, which housed the Sigma Pi fraternity headquarters from 2013 to 2019, was sold to the city that year. Residents 65 or older make up 16.2% of the population and 30.8% of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher. Retail sales reached about $3.48 billion in 2022 and median household income is $72,848 for 2020-2024, per Census QuickFacts.

sections.h2: Which schools serve a Lebanon address?
sections.html:
Lebanon Special School District covers most of the city for pre-kindergarten through eighth grade. Its Director of Schools page reports about 4,600 students, five elementary schools (Byars Dowdy, Castle Heights, Coles Ferry, Jones Brummett and Sam Houston) and two middle schools, Walter J. Baird and Winfree Bryant.

High school students are zoned to Wilson County Schools, which also serves a few small parts of Lebanon for all grades. District lines decide a buyer's school, so tell buyers to confirm an address with the district and not rely on a listing description. LSSD offers an address search tool on its own site.

sections.h2: Does Lebanon's weather matter when preparing a house for sale?
sections.html:
Lebanon's summers are humid and its winters mild. Wikipedia's NOAA-based table lists a July average high near 90 degrees (90.2), about 54 inches of rain and melted snow spread over roughly 117 wet days, and just 1.5 inches of snowfall. Extremes on record run from 111 degrees down to minus 20.

That pattern puts the stress on roofs, gutters, grading and cooling equipment more than on freeze damage. A roof and drainage check before you weigh an offer shows you what the other side's inspector will raise.

sections.h2: How do Lebanon city and Wilson County property taxes work?
sections.html:
Lebanon taxes each house once for the city and once for Wilson County, and the two bills have different payment points. The City of Lebanon shows a rate of $0.4054 on each $100 of assessed value, collected at the city property tax office at 200 N. Castle Heights Avenue.

Lebanon and Wilson County tax calendar (City of Lebanon and Wilson County Assessor)
DateEvent
January 1Assessment date for all property
May 20Assessor notes assessments on the roll and notifies owners of changes
June 1County Board of Equalization begins hearing appeals
August 1State appeal filing deadline, unless 45 days after the county board's ruling falls later
October 1 to February 28City taxes payable without penalty
March 1City penalty starts at 1.5% per month

The assessor puts the value on the house and the state prints the city notices, so send address corrections to 615-444-8661. County bills go out in mid-October, and the Wilson County Trustee at 228 E. Main Street, Room 102 takes payment through the end of February.

sections.h2: What can a Lebanon owner do about a high assessment before selling?
sections.html:
Start with a call or visit to the Wilson County Property Assessor, because many disputes are clerical. The assessor's appeal page says the next step is Wilson County's Board of Equalization, a panel of five property owners with one seat from Lebanon, one from Mt. Juliet and three from the county.

The board convenes June 1 and stays in session until that year's work is finished, with a newspaper notice from the assessor about ten days earlier. Hearing slots are normally booked by phone or at the counter during late May or early June. You may appear yourself, send a relative or attorney, and bring witnesses. A lower assessed value helps the next owner, so pursue the appeal before you list if the number looks wrong.

sections.h2: Who handles permits, short-term rentals and building rules in Lebanon?
sections.html:
The city's planning and building departments split the work. Zoning enforcement officials handle pools, fences, sidewalks and short-term rental permits, and they also staff the Board of Zoning Appeals for setback variances and accessory structure variances, per the Long Range Planning page. Zoning staff also support the Historic Zoning Commission, which handles certificates of appropriateness.

  • Building permits and inspections come from the Chief Building Official's staff, who hold ICC and state certifications.
  • Electrical inspections are not done by the city. State of Tennessee deputy electrical inspectors do them.
  • New single-family and townhome projects follow a five-step residential development process before a certificate of occupancy is issued.

A house once rented to short-term guests deserves a call to the zoning office at 615-444-3647 to find out what permit is on file.

sections.h2: How is a Lebanon sale recorded?
sections.html:
A Lebanon deed is filed with the Wilson County Register of Deeds. The state charges 37 cents in transfer tax on each $100 of price, per the revenue department, which comes to about $1,400 on a sale at the city's $378,400 median value.

Owners over 65 or disabled may have state and county tax relief, and seniors may qualify for the tax freeze on a primary residence, both run by the Wilson County Trustee at 615-444-0894 (option 2). Ask the Trustee how a sale during the year affects either program.

faqs.q: Is a Lebanon house with tenants still sellable?
faqs.a: Yes. Hand the buyer a copy of the lease early and ask the title company how it affects closing. A purchaser taking the house as-is can accept a rented property, and the tenant's plans can be settled in the contract.

faqs.q: When are Lebanon city property taxes due?
faqs.a: City taxes can be paid from October 1 through February 28. After that, the City of Lebanon adds a penalty of 1.5% a month starting March 1.

faqs.q: Who decides what my Lebanon house is worth for taxes?
faqs.a: The Wilson County Property Assessor sets it. The city multiplies its own rate against that value, and a dispute goes to the assessor first and the Board of Equalization second.

faqs.q: Is there a tax freeze for older Lebanon homeowners?
faqs.a: Yes. Wilson County's Trustee operates a freeze that holds a senior's tax amount on a primary residence, plus a relief program covering older, disabled and disabled veteran owners. Call 615-444-0894 and choose option 2.

faqs.q: Does the city inspect electrical work on a Lebanon house?
faqs.a: No. Electrical inspections are done by State of Tennessee deputy inspectors, not by the Lebanon Building Inspection Department.
